config.title: React advanced patterns

intro.title: React advanced patterns
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that uses the render props pattern to share functionality. You'll learn how to pass a function as a prop to a component, allowing it to render dynamic content based on shared logic. The main technologies involved are React components, props, and functions in JavaScript. This pattern helps make your components more reusable and flexible, which is a key skill in frontend development.
intro.usecase: Advanced React patterns like render props, higher-order components, and custom hooks are essential in building scalable enterprise applications. You'll see them in complex dashboards like Salesforce or Google Analytics, where reusable data-fetching logic and component composition manage real-time metrics across multiple panels. E-commerce platforms like Shopify use these patterns for checkout flows that combine address forms, payment modals, and inventory validation into maintainable, decoupled components. Mastering these patterns helps you build UIs that remain performant and extensible as product requirements evolve.

objectives: Implement a controlled component to manage form state in React
Construct a custom hook to encapsulate and reuse stateful logic
Apply the Context API to share data across multiple components
Configure a higher-order component to enhance component functionality
Manipulate component rendering using conditional logic and lists
Integrate prop types for runtime type checking in components
Initialize and update state using the useState hook in functional components

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added, allowing you to use React and state in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named App that returns JSX containing a <div> with no content inside.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the component is named exactly 'App' and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you defined a function named App that returns a div element.

steps.title: Initialize state for a counter
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to create a state variable named 'count' initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value 0 and destructure the returned array into count and setCount.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state initialization
const [value, setValue] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a count state variable initialized to 0.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with 0 as the initial value, and the returned array is destructured into count and setCount.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with 0 as the initial value and destructuring the array into count and setCount.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use the useState hook to create a state variable named count initialized to 0.

steps.title: Define an increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named handleIncrement that updates the count state by incrementing it by 1.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setCount with the current count plus 1. You can use the previous state to calculate the new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a handleIncrement function that increments the count state when called.
successCriteria: A function named handleIncrement is defined inside the App component and it updates the count state by incrementing it by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named handleIncrement and properly increments the count state by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleIncrement function isn't defined correctly. Check that it's inside the App component and updates the count state.

steps.title: Define a decrement handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleDecrement that updates the count state by decreasing it by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setCount state setter to update count to count - 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleDecrement function is added to the component, which when called will decrement the count state by 1.
successCriteria: The component contains a function named handleDecrement that uses setCount to update the count state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a function, but make sure it's named handleDecrement and correctly updates the count state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleDecrement function is missing or doesn't properly decrement the count state.

steps.title: Add a heading to display the counter value
steps.instruction: In your component's return statement, add an h1 element that displays the current count value.
steps.hint: Use JSX to create an h1 element and embed the count state variable inside curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a value in JSX

Current value: {someState}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render an h1 heading showing the current count value (initially 0).
successCriteria: An h1 element is added to the return statement, and it displays the count state variable using curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an h1 element, but make sure it displays the count variable using curly braces like {count}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading isn't displaying the count value correctly. Check that you're using the count variable inside curly braces in the h1 element.

steps.title: Add an increment button and wire its onClick
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Increment' inside the return statement, and set its onClick prop to call the handleIncrement function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the heading. Use the onClick attribute with the handler function name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with a click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Increment' appears below the heading, and clicking it will eventually increase the counter when the handler is defined.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Increment' is added, and its onClick prop is set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text 'Increment' and the onClick is set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly configured. Add a <button> with text 'Increment' and onClick={handleIncrement}.

steps.title: Add a decrement button and wire its onClick
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Decrement' and wire its onClick event to the handleDecrement function.
steps.hint: Add a button element inside the fragment, similar to the increment button but with different text and onClick handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: adding a button with onClick handler
<button onClick={handleAction}>Action</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have a second button labeled 'Decrement' that decreases the counter when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Decrement' is added, and its onClick attribute calls handleDecrement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement button is missing or not properly wired. Check the button element and onClick attribute.

steps.title: Add a reset handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleReset that sets the count state back to 0.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with 0 as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleReset function that resets the count to 0 when called.
successCriteria: The handleReset function is defined and calls setCount(0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named handleReset and calls setCount(0).
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to define a function named handleReset that sets count to 0.

steps.title: Add a reset button and wire its onClick
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Reset' and wire its onClick event to the handleReset function you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element after the decrement button. Use onClick={handleReset} to connect it to your reset handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with an event handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A third button labeled 'Reset' appears in the UI, and clicking it resets the counter to 0.
successCriteria: A button with the text 'Reset' is added to the JSX, and its onClick prop is set to handleReset.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the text 'Reset' and its onClick is wired to handleReset.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button is missing or not properly connected. Add a <button> element with onClick={handleReset} and the text 'Reset'.
